terms.grammar: relative pronoun, with a verb of its own; neuter quicquid
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 309b: Quisquis homō hūc profectō vēnerit, pugnōs edet.
Sen. Ep. 20.13: quisquis exit in lūcem
terms.comment: Quisquis es, whoever you are, is the polite way to address a stranger (Plaut. Men. 278b). “Anyone who” in a condition is often sī quis (see “someone”).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.31.3: quīcumque is est, eī mē profiteor inimīcum

phrases.latin: Quisquis homō hūc profectō vēnerit, pugnōs edet.
phrases.english: Whoever comes this way, believe me, will get a taste of my fists.
Heaven bless you, whoever you are.

phrases.latin: Quisquis es, quidquid tibi nōmen est, senex
phrases.english: Whoever you are, whatever your name is, old man

phrases.latin: nēmō nāscitur dīves; quisquis exit in lūcem jussus est lacte et pannō esse contentus
phrases.english: no one is born rich; whoever comes into the light is told to be content with milk and a rag
